# id mapping tables (WoG/H3 ↔ Olden Era)

The plugin reads `*.json` from `BepInEx/config/WoG/id-maps/` (`tools/deploy/deploy.ps1` copies this folder there). The
files hold only ids and numbers — no game data — so they are committed; the generated ones are rebuilt from the
user's `Core.zip` after a game update. A row with `engine: null` is not mapped: ERM commands with such an id report
*unsupported* and nothing is substituted.

* `creature.json` — two-way, `{"wog": H3/WoG creature number, "engine": Olden Era unit sid | null, …}`; generated by
  `WoG.ErmTool idmap-creatures <Core.zip> <creature.json>` (`tools/WoG.ErmTool/CreatureMap.cs`):
  * H3 town → Olden Era faction by theme: Castle → human (Temple), Rampart → nature (Grove), Necropolis → undead,
    Dungeon → dungeon, Inferno → demon (Hive), Conflux → unfrozen (Schism); Tower, Stronghold and Fortress have no
    Olden Era faction and stay unmapped;
  * H3 level L: the base creature → the faction's tier-L base unit, the upgrade → its `_upg` unit;
  * neutrals with the same creature: halfling, peasant, fairie dragon;
  * every Olden Era unit without an H3 number (`_upg_alt`, Olden Era neutrals) gets a number from 1000 up; numbers given
    before are kept.
* `resource.json` — two-way: wood 0, mercury 1, ore 2, sulfur 3 (none in Olden Era), crystals 4, gemstones 5, gold 6.
* `skill.json` — two-way, written by hand: H3 secondary skill (Format SS) → Olden Era hero skill sid, chosen by effect
  (Logistics → `skill_logistic`, Luck → `skill_luck`, Necromancy → `skill_faction_undead`, Estates → `skill_economy`,
  Learning → `skill_enlightenment`, Offense → `skill_assault`, Armorer → `skill_protection`, …; 14 of 28). H3 skills
  without an equivalent (`"engine": null`: Pathfinding, Archery, Navigation, Wisdom, Mysticism, Eagle Eye, the four
  magic schools, Scholar, Artillery, Intelligence, First Aid) read as not learned; Olden Era-only skills get numbers
  from 1000 up and are not shown to scripts.
* `spell.json` — two-way, written by hand (`"engine"` checked against `DB/magics`): H3 spell 0..69 → Olden Era spell
  sid, chosen by effect (Magic Arrow → `bonus_magic_pure_bolt`, Bless → `day_2_magic_sharp_edge` "more basic attack
  damage", Slow → `night_2_magic_web` "less speed", Blind → `night_8_magic_sleep`, Fly → `neutral_magic_shadow_form`,
  …; 37 of 70). Spells without an equivalent (boats, elemental schools and protections, morale and luck, elemental
  summons, …) read as not known. A specialist knows a spell as its `_special` variant, which is the same number. Olden
  Era-only spells get numbers from 1000 up.

When a saved game is loaded, the tables of these files replace the copies stored in its WoG state (the files may be
newer than the save); numbers given during the game (hero numbers) come from the save.
* `object.json` — one-way, `{"engine": object sid, "tag", "type", "subtype", "h3", "note"}`: an Olden Era map object →
  H3 object type/subtype (ERM "Format OB"); several Olden Era objects may stand for one H3 type, and placing an H3
  type uses its first sid. Generated by `WoG.ErmTool idmap-objects <Core.zip> <object.json> [artifact.json]`
  (`tools/WoG.ErmTool/ObjectMap.cs`) from `DB/map/objects`:
  * the equivalent is chosen by what the object does (`DB/objects_logic`), not by its name: mines by `resName`,
    windmill (resources weekly) → Windmill 112, watchtower (reveals the fog) → Redwood Observatory 58, mana well →
    Magic Well 49, market → Trading Post 99, forge (sells items) → Black Market 7, sacrificial shrine → Altar of
    Sacrifice 2, hero's crypt → Crypt 84, stables → Stables 94, …;
  * `custom_X` (generator variants with other rewards) maps like `X`;
  * cities by faction as for creatures (type 98, Format T), dwellings `barracks_<faction>_<tier>` → the town dwelling of
    that level (type 17, Format CG), portals `portal_N…` → Two-Way Monolith N−1 (type 45), artifacts → type 5
    (subtype from `artifact.json` when it exists, else −1);
  * every other interactive Olden Era object gets a type from 1000 up (sid order, kept between runs); scenery
    (environment, animals, effects, blocks) is not an ERM object and is not listed.
  Monster squads (type 54) and heroes on the map (type 34) are not in this file: the adapter adds them from the game
  state (a squad of several unit types counts as its first unit, through `creature.json`).
